items.text: Process tree is correct: Utilman.exe /debug (no process-create event) → osk.exe (rec 18917) → whoami.exe (rec 18918), with LogonUI.exe's registry event (rec 18916) kept out of the chain
Spotted that osk.exe's Description is 'Windows Command Processor' and concluded the On-Screen Keyboard file had been replaced with cmd.exe (accessibility-features backdoor)
Explained Utilman.exe /debug as the Ease of Access manager started from the logon screen, so Utilman → osk is normal by itself and the abnormal part is what osk.exe really is

Explained SYSTEM (LogonId 0x3e7, System integrity) in session 2 as a shell on the logon screen with no authentication, so 'nobody was logged on' is consistent with the attack rather than evidence of a false positive
Treated the RuleName tags (e.g. T1076 Remote Desktop Protocol) as config labels rather than evidence, and said the LogonUI event suggests a logon screen or RDP session without proving it
Distinguished replaced file from IFEO Debugger using Image and Description, and said the backdoor was planted earlier, outside the export, by someone who already had admin rights
Recognised the host as a domain controller and explained why SYSTEM there means likely domain compromise
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. when and how osk.exe was replaced, the RDP source, what was typed after whoami, other backdoored hosts)
Classified it as a true positive (Critical), escalated it as an active domain compromise, and recommended preserving the binaries, finding the RDP source, checking other DCs, and requiring NLA
